ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the beaker on the left is an Ag electrode immersed in 1.0 M AgNO3 solution, and the beaker on the right is a Sn electrode immersed in 1.0 M Sn(NO3)2 solution. The two beakers are connected by a salt bridge and are connected to a voltmeter. The table below the figure lists half-reactions, among which the reduction half-reaction of tin is Sn2+ + 2e- -> Sn(s). Reasoning: The problem gives the mass of tin deposited as 1.65 g and the time as 10.0 min. Taking the molar mass of tin as 118.7 g/mol, n(Sn)=1.65/118.7=0.0139 mol. From the half-reaction, each formation of 1 mol Sn requires 2 mol electrons, so n(e-)=2×0.0139=0.0278 mol. The amount of charge Q=nF=0.0278×96485 C=approximately 2.68×10^3 C. The time 10.0 min=600 s, so the current I=Q/t=2680/600=4.47 A.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: note the Sn electrode is in a solution labeled 1.0 M Sn(NO3)2. From the formula Sn(NO3)2, infer tin ions are Sn^{2+}; plating Sn(s) therefore consumes 2 electrons per atom.
